subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview treat all syntactically complete identifier and member-expression assignment values as safe references, or preserve a narrower fail-closed rule?
rationale: The false positive is well supported, but broadening what bypasses secret-like assignment detection changes a security boundary and requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept Pure References
options.body: Exempt syntactically complete identifiers and member expressions regardless of root name while retaining all literal and concrete-token checks.

options.title: Expand Selected Forms
options.body: Add only specific roots or reference shapes, retaining naming-dependent false positives in exchange for a smaller scanner change.

options.title: Add An Override
options.body: Introduce configuration or a CLI escape hatch that redacts or bypasses findings, creating a broader operator-controlled exception.

recommendation.title: Accept Pure References
recommendation.body: Exempt syntactically complete identifiers and member expressions regardless of root name while retaining all literal and concrete-token checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Their immediately preceding merged work defines the current fail-closed scanner boundary and associated hardening coverage.
